supplementary_news.content: ___ × Market Information Top Poultry Companies Expert Insights Blogs Regions Magazines Sign In Poultry Meat Egg Poultry Health Sustainability Poultry Future Chicken Marketing Summit Poultry Tech Summit Broilers & Turkeys Diseases & Health Avian Influenza Avian flu cases confirmed in poultry in 5 European states As the northern hemisphere fall reaches its peak, a handful of new outbreaks of highly pathogenic avian influenza involving domestic birds have been reported, while further infections in the wild population have been detected more widely across Europe. Jackie Linden October 12, 2026 mashi_naz | Bigstock Article Summary Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) outbreaks involving H5 viruses have been confirmed in poultry across five European countries—Belgium, Bulgaria, France, Germany, and the United Kingdom—over the past month, with hundreds of thousands of birds affected and 316 total farm outbreaks reported across Europe in 2026. Five European nations have confirmed HPAI outbreaks in poultry involving H5 family viruses since September 2026 Bulgaria reported 41,000 affected birds across two farms, bringing the nation's 12-month total to 18 outbreaks 2026 European totals show 316 poultry outbreaks in 16 countries, compared to 729 outbreaks across 23 countries in all of 2025 H5N1 virus variant dominates confirmed cases, with Poland leading at 143 outbreaks, followed by Germany with 40 Wild bird infections continue spreading with 2,709 HPAI outbreaks logged across Europe in 2026, primarily involving H5N1 Over the past month, new outbreaks of highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) in poultry involving viruses of the H5 family have occurred in Belgium, Bulgaria, France, Germany and the United Kingdom (U.K.). In Bulgaria, the H5N1 HPAI virus serotype has been detected at two more poultry farms in the central province of Plovdiv since mid-September, based on notifications to the World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH). Affected at the first premises were 8,000 mallard ducks, followed by around 33,000 laying hens at the second location in the first week of October. These bring the nation’s total over the past 12 months to 18. Also confirming to WOAH two recent infections with this virus variant was France. Both those affected were commercial flocks in the department of Maine-et-Loire, and started in the first week of September. The first involved 2,500 vaccinated ducks, and the second close to 10,000 breeding ducks that had not been vaccinated against HPAI. Three French outbreaks have been reported since the end of August, all in Maine-et-Loire, which is located in the western region of Pays de la Loire. Great Britain’s HPAI outbreak total in poultry has increased to 20 following the detection of the H5N5 virus in the first days of October. Testing positive was a small backyard flock on the Isle of Lewis, according to the same source. Part of the Western Isles, Lewis is located off the northwestern coast of Scotland. Meanwhile, the veterinary authorities of Belgium and Germany have each reported to WOAH outbreaks linked to the H5N1 virus in captive birds. The Belgian outbreaks affected around 450 birds in mixed flocks in the Limburg and Antwerp areas, while the German outbreak in the northeast of the country is reported retrospectively, having started in May. Farm outbreak total approaches 320 So far in 2026, 16 countries in the region have confirmed a total of 316 HPAI outbreaks in poultry, according to the latest update of the Animal Disease Information System from the European Commission (EC; as of October 7). The database monitors listed animal diseases in European Union member states and selected adjacent countries (but not Great Britain). At each of the affected premises this year, presence of the H5N1 virus variant has been confirmed. For comparison, 729 outbreaks in these flocks were reported by 23 countries during the whole of 2025. This year, Poland’s total remains the highest to date at 143 although it has not changed since May. Next come Germany (40) and France (23). Including backyard poultry, ornamental flocks, zoos, and similar premises, the EC’s System monitors HPAI cases in “captive birds” in a separate category. To date in 2026, 15 countries have notified the System of 123 outbreaks involving captive birds. During the whole of last year, 25 countries registered 175 outbreaks in this category with the EC. HPAI-related developments affecting Europe’s poultry sector Based on the changing HPAI situation in the region, Germany’s veterinary reference laboratory Friedrich-Loeffler Institute has raised the disease risk level for the nation’s poultry flocks. The risk is now seen as “moderate” for both the transmission of H5 viruses to poultry and captive birds directly or indirectly from the wild population, and between wild birds within the country. Last month, EU member states agreed with a proposal from the European Commission Directorate for Agriculture, DG Agriculture and Rural Development (DG-AGRI) to release funds from the agricultural reserve to compensate Italian farmers hit by previous HPAI outbreaks. EUR61 million (US$68 million) will be directed to poultry and egg farmers whose businesses were impacted by measures taken to control and prevent the spread of infection between September of 2022 and March of 2025. Payments must be made to the recipients by May of next year. More widespread HPAI cases in wild birds As of October 7, a total of 2,709 HPAI outbreaks in Europe’s wild population had been logged by the EC’s System by 33 countries in 2026. Of these, the H5N1 virus serotype was involved in around 2,660, while the rest were identified as belonging to the H5 group. Based on EC data, wild birds infected with the H5N1 variant have been recorded by Denmark, Germany, the Netherlands, Norway and Sweden over the past month. Following a hiatus of around 18 months, the same virus was detected again on the Mediterranean island of Cyprus in September, according to a recent WOAH notification. The same agency has been notified about the first wild birds that have tested positive for H5N1 since the start of the HPAI “season.” Six birds were found dead at four locations in England. Over the past month, WOAH has been informed about seven wild birds in Iceland that have tested positive for the H5N5 virus serotype. Antarctica: A Transcriptomic Study Showing Limited Host-Species Effect 【字体: 大 中 小 】 时间:2026年10月15日 来源:Viruses 3.5 编辑推荐: 在第41次中国南极考察(2024–2025)期间,研究人员从Ardley岛同域分布的Adélie企鹅、帽带企鹅(chinstrap penguins)和巴布亚企鹅(gentoo penguins)采集新鲜粪便样本。通过转录组测序(transcriptomic 欢迎领取《类器官应用方案 3D之旅》 为了促进科学的传播,生物通采集了这篇文章 订阅BioHot点这里解锁原文链接推送! “畅读会员”点此登录查看原文链接 Article Open access 在第41次中国南极考察(2024–2025)期间,研究人员从Ardley岛同域分布的Adélie企鹅、帽带企鹅(chinstrap penguins)和巴布亚企鹅(gentoo penguins)采集新鲜粪便样本。通过转录组测序(transcriptomic sequencing)结合病毒contig组装,系统分析了粪便病毒组(faecal viromes)。共注释到32个已知病毒科(viral families),但超过一半的病毒reads仍未分类,表明南极企鹅肠道中存在大量未表征的病毒多样性(uncharacterised viral diversity)。未检测到病毒丰度或α多样性(alpha-diversity)的显著种间差异,宿主物种(host-species)对病毒群落结构仅产生微弱影响。虽然未检测到H5N1高致病性禽流感(H5N1 highly pathogenic avian influenza)和新城疫病毒(Newcastle disease virus),但回收了若干潜在病原体,包括δ冠状病毒(deltacoronaviruses)、新型星状病毒(novel astroviruses)和小RNA病毒(picornaviruses)。该工作为南极Pygoscelis企鹅建立了基线病毒组数据,并为极地野生动物长期病原监测和病毒溢出风险(viral spillover risk)评估提供了有价值见解。 论文主体部分解读 瑞孚迪自动化解决方案>>领 取 研究背景方面,Ardley岛位于南极半岛西部Fildes Peninsula区域,毗邻南设得兰群岛的King George Island,是海洋性南极最大无冰区之一。与南极大陆相比,该岛相对温和的温度和较多降水维持了多样筑巢海鸟种群和广泛植被。三种同域Pygoscelis企鹅,即Adélie、gentoo和chinstrap企鹅,在该岛繁殖。长期宿主–病毒共进化使这些企鹅维持低致病性病毒的稳定储库,包括禽流感病毒、星状病毒(astroviruses)、副黏病毒(paramyxoviruses)、圆环病毒(circoviruses)、腺病毒(adenoviruses)和多瘤病毒(polyomaviruses)。尽管病毒检测报告不断增加,但同域物种间病毒组组成和种间病毒多样性的系统比较仍然缺乏,这受限于样本量小和病毒覆盖不完整。为填补该知识空白,研究人员在2024年12月至2025年4月采集三种Pygoscelis企鹅新鲜粪便样本,利用转录组测序、病毒contig组装和分类注释,表征病毒群落、种间病毒多样性以及高风险病原分布,从而为极地生态系统长期野生动物监测和生态风险评估建立基线病毒组数据集。 研究人员开展的研究表明,共获得32个合格粪便转录组样本,其中14份来自Adélie企鹅、9份来自chinstrap企鹅、9份来自gentoo企鹅。研究共注释到32个已知病毒科,超过一半病毒reads未分类。病毒丰度和α多样性无显著种间差异,宿主物种对病毒群落结构仅呈弱效应。所有样本均未检测到H5N1 HPAIV或新城疫病毒(Newcastle disease virus, NDV)。同时,研究人员回收了若干潜在病原体,包括δ冠状病毒(deltacoronaviruses)、新型星状病毒(novel astroviruses)和小RNA病毒(picornaviruses)。该研究为南极Pygoscelis企鹅建立基线病毒组数据,并为极地野生动物长期病原监测和病毒溢出风险(viral spillover risk)评估提供重要依据。 为开展研究,关键技术方法如下:样本队列来源为2024年12月至2025年4月在Ardley岛采集的Adélie、chinstrap和gentoo企鹅新鲜粪便,样本以RNAlater保存于?80 °C;宿主物种通过形态特征和线粒体COI基因序列比对确认。提取总RNA后建库,并在DNBSEQ-T7平台进行PE 150 bp测序。使用FastQC和Trimmomatic质控,MEGAHIT进行从头组装,DIAMOND-BLASTX和BLASTN搜索NCBI nr/nt数据库,E值设为10?10,Bowtie2、SAMtools和CoverM定量TPM。多样性分析采用Kruskal–Wallis检验、Bray–Curtis距离、PERMANOVA、NMDS、PCoA和Ward聚类;系统发育分析采用MAFFT、IQ-TREE最大似然法(ML)1000次bootstrap、FigTree和pheatmap。 研究结果如下。 3.1 样本采集与宿主物种组成(Sample Collection and Host Species Composition):样本采集于Ardley岛邻近中国长城站的区域,时间为2024年12月至2025年2月。研究人员对chinstrap、Adélie和gentoo企鹅新鲜粪便进行总核酸提取、文库制备和转录组测序,共获得32个合格粪便转录组样本。结合野外形态观察和线粒体COI基因序列比对确认宿主物种,样本包括14份Adélie企鹅、9份chinstrap企鹅和9份gentoo企鹅。 3.2 粪便样本病毒群落组成与多样性(Composition and Diversity of Viral Communities in Faecal Samples):32个粪便转录组文库完成测序,质控后各样本clean reads为38.33百万至75.50百万,平均54.77百万,测序深度足以进行病毒组表征。研究共识别32个已知病毒科;去除噬菌体和逆转录病毒后,保留23个已知真核病毒种用于下游分析。未分类序列占三种宿主所有病毒reads的一半以上,表明南极企鹅肠道生态系统存在大量未描述病毒多样性。注释病毒包括RNA和DNA病毒群。主要RNA病毒类群包括Picornaviridae、Coronaviridae、Astroviridae、Paramyxoviridae和Rountreeviridae;Picornaviridae在chinstrap和Adélie企鹅中较gentoo企鹅更丰富,Coronaviridae在Adélie企鹅中高度富集;藻类和植物来源RNA病毒也被检测到,被认为来自企鹅饮食摄入。主要DNA病毒包括Herpesviridae、Adenoviridae和Poxviridae,以及巨型DNA病毒(Pandoraviridae、Mimiviridae、Schizomimiviridae);Herpesviridae在chinstrap企鹅中偏好积累,巨型DNA病毒在gentoo企鹅中丰度较高;藻类和植物DNA病毒(Phycodnaviridae、Caulimoviridae)也被鉴定为食源性污染物。所有粪便样本均未检测到H5N1 HPAIV或NDV。α多样性方面,基于物种丰富度和Shannon指数的Kruskal–Wallis检验显示,三种企鹅间病毒物种丰富度(p = 0.085)和Shannon多样性(p = 0.294)无显著差异。β多样性方面,基于Bray–Curtis距离的PCoA前两轴累计解释29.5%总变异(PCoA1为18.5%,PCoA2为11.1%),NMDS结果一致(Stress = 0.227);PERMANOVA检测到宿主物种对病毒群落结构有统计学显著影响(R2 = 0.097,p = 0.021),但低R2值表明宿主过滤作用弱,宿主物种不驱动形成物种特异性病毒组。多数样本间组成差异来自宿主个体特征、饮食差异、环境暴露和随机过程。 3.3 Adélie企鹅来源δ冠状病毒基因组与系统发育特征(Genomic and Phylogenetic Characteristics of Adélie Penguin-Derived Deltacoronavirus):研究人员从单个Adélie企鹅粪便样本1227-13成功组装近完整δ冠状病毒基因组,长度为26,196 nt。该病毒被正式命名为“Adélie penguin deltacoronavirus”。基于trimmed基因组序列和RNA依赖的RNA聚合酶(RdRp)复制酶基因序列构建最大似然系统发育树,结果显示该株属于Coronaviridae的Buldecovirus亚属,并与2023年从南极鞘嘴鸟中回收的δ冠状病毒以及2014年最初在gentoo企鹅中鉴定的δ冠状病毒序列聚类。基因组比较显示,该分离株与2023年南极鞘嘴鸟δ冠状病毒(GenBank accession: PQ351810.1)核苷酸同一性最高,为96.23%。基于RdRp的系统发育分析表明,极地δ冠状病毒分离株与其它大陆禽类群体中流行的δ冠状病毒存在显著遗传分化。这些发现提示δ冠状病毒在南极海鸟间持续跨种传播,并出现独特的南极δ冠状病毒谱系。 3.4 企鹅星状病毒基因组与系统发育特征(Genomic and Phylogenetic Characteristics of Penguin Astrovirus):研究人员回收了近全长星状病毒基因组,编码ORF1a、ORF1b(RdRp)和ORF2衣壳蛋白。基于RdRp和衣壳蛋白氨基酸序列分别构建系统发育树,并辅以序列同一性热图分析。系统发育分析将该分离株置于Avastrovirus属,正式命名为“Penguin astrovirus 2025”。先前报道的南极星状病毒在树上分散,未能形成单一单系极地进化枝。同源分析显示,该企鹅分离株的RdRp和ORF2序列与来自其它大陆的代表性星状病毒株相比,序列同一性显著低于公认星状病毒种界定阈值(RdRp核苷酸为83%,衣壳蛋白为75%)。因此,该分离株被提议代表一个新的星状病毒种。 3.5 企鹅Picornaviridae和Caliciviridae基因组与系统发育特征(Genomic and Phylogenetic Characteristics of Penguin Picornaviridae and Caliciviridae):除Coronaviridae和Astroviridae外,病毒组分析显示Picornaviridae和Caliciviridae是企鹅粪便样本中丰富的病毒组分,并组装到多个归属这两个科的病毒contig。基于推导的RdRp氨基酸序列分别构建Picornaviridae和Caliciviridae最大似然系统发育树。Picornaviridae序列分散于该科多个属,包括Hepatovirus、Megrivirus及若干未分类picorna-like viruses,反映高谱系多样性;其中若干病毒进化枝与禽、海洋哺乳动物和蝙蝠宿主来源病毒近缘。四个Caliciviridae序列聚类在Goosecalicivirus进化枝内,并形成两个明显亚簇,与鹅来源禽类calicivirus系统发育关系最近,且与Caliciviridae内其它属明显分离。主要分支获得稳健节点bootstrap支持。 讨论部分总结:该研究系统表征了三种同域南极企鹅的粪便病毒组,识别32个已知病毒科,其中超过一半序列仍未分类。该高比例未分类序列表明南极企鹅肠道生态系统是丰富且仍大量未描述病毒多样性的储库。公共病毒参考数据库不完整,加上短读长转录组数据,限制了许多新型病毒contig的准确分类注释。病毒丰度和α多样性在物种间无显著差异。β多样性分析表明宿主物种显著影响病毒群落组成,但低决定系数提示宿主物种密度对病毒群落结构贡献有限。病毒群落大多数变异来自个体特征、饮食变异、环境暴露和随机生态过程。饮食来源的藻类和植物相关病毒频繁回收,进一步说明食物资源对肠道病毒组谱的影响。虽然未检测到H5N1或NDV等高致病性病毒,但鉴于采样范围和样本量受限,不能完全排除感染可能性。南极企鹅粪便病毒组中多个病毒科,包括Picornaviridae、Coronaviridae、Astroviridae和Caliciviridae,与温带家禽和其它禽类宿主常见肠道病毒群重叠。这支持一套核心病毒科在Aves中跨地理远距离区域广泛传播的观点。然而,许多南极病毒contig与温带禽类对应序列存在显著序列分化,提示病毒定殖南极生态系统后发生局部适应进化。与先前发现一致,Picornaviridae和Astroviridae构成企鹅粪便样本中主要RNA病毒组分。值得注意的是,本研究表征的δ冠状病毒是首个从Adélie企鹅获得的近完整δ冠状病毒基因组。系统发育分析确认该病毒聚类于先前鉴定的南极海鸟δ冠状病毒谱系,支持δ冠状病毒可能在同域南极海鸟间经历反复跨种传播事件的假设。对于本研究表征的新型星状病毒,基于RdRp和衣壳蛋白的系统发育构建显示南极星状病毒呈多系分布。具体而言,Penguin astrovirus 2025聚类于禽类家禽和水禽相关的Avastrovirus Clade 1,而先前报道的Adélie企鹅星状病毒(KM587711)属于一个不同系统发育进化枝。该模式提示星状病毒谱系多次独立引入南极企鹅种群,而非单一古老极地地方性星状病毒祖先。同源重组是塑造Astroviridae成员遗传多样性的已确立进化力量。鉴于本研究数据集范围,未进行专门重组检测分析。这是本研究在物种界定和进化推断方面的关键限制。不过,分类归属得到两个独立遗传标记(RdRp和衣壳蛋白)支持,部分缓解了重组事件可能带来的系统发育混杂信号。尽管检测到的病毒主要引起无症状潜伏感染且当前无疫情暴发,其溢出风险仍不可忽视。外来病原的引入可驱动适应性突变、毒力增强和跨种传播。此外,高密度繁殖群和候鸟活动可能加速病毒在南极野生动物间的传播,可能破坏极地生态系统。因此,建立长期系统性病原监测对于追踪病毒动态和保障极地生态安全至关重要。 Gastroenterology Ear, Nose and Throat Emergency Care Endocrinology Heart - Cardiology and Cardiovascular Surgery Liver Diseases Neurology Neurosurgery Nursing Obstetrics and Gynecology Ophthalmology Orthopedics Pain Management Pediatrics Primary Care Psychiatry Radiology Surgery Thoracic Surgery Transplantation Services Urgent Care Urology View All Services About Us About Us About Us View More Clinical Ethics Consult Services Contact Us Digital Patient Tools and Resources Executive Leadership Facts and Figures Financial Assistance Insurance Information International Patient Services LGBT Health at the Mount Sinai Health System Language Access Services Mount Sinai Daily Mount Sinai Doctors Medical Records Medical Staff Services Department MyMountSinai® App Newsroom The Mount Sinai Health Network Our Mission Quality & Patient Safety Pay My Bill Physician Access Services Sustain Mount Sinai Visit Us Office for Health Data, Outcomes, and Engagement Strategy View More Search Close Clear Submit 1-800-MD-SINAI1-800-MD-SINAI MyMountSinai (MyChart) Check Symptoms & Get Care Pay My Bill For Physicians Same-Day Appointments Make a Gift Home About Us Newsroom Press Release Mount Sinai Awarded Five-Year, $20.7 Million Vaccine Development Agreement to Advance Next-Generation Technologies Against Respiratory Threats Project will begin with an H5N1 flu vaccine prototype and development of a vaccine platform framework for broader, safer, and more durable immune protection Credit: Brittainy Newman for Mount Sinai Health System New York, NY (October 13, 2026) Researchers at the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai have been awarded a five-year project agreement to develop Vaccine Immunoengineering for Targeted Antigen Presentation and Layered Control (VITAL), a research program exploring an improved approach to vaccination against respiratory pathogens. The project is supported by the Defense Threat Reduction Agency’s Joint Science and Technology Office (JSTO) through the Medical CBRN Defense Consortium. The agreement has a total estimated project cost of approximately $20.7 million over its period of performance, with funding provided incrementally. VITAL was selected under Reimagining Available Vaccines and Envisioning Novelty (RAVEN), a JSTO program focused on advancing multivalent prophylactic biological countermeasures. RAVEN seeks both improvements to existing technologies and new vaccine or preventive platforms capable of addressing multiple biological threats, moving beyond approaches that are focused on one threat at a time. The initial proof of concept will focus on a highly pathogenic avian influenza A virus, H5N1. ​​Researchers will develop an unmodified mRNA-based vaccine prototype designed for intranasal delivery that will restrict primarily the immunogen expression to immune cells known as macrophages in the respiratory tract, avoiding potential adverse events by expression of the antigen in other type of cells that do not participate in this process during natural infection. The program will evaluate how this targeting affects antigen presentation, immune stimulation, safety, and protection. “VITAL is designed to directly support RAVEN’s objective by asking a broader question than whether we can make a vaccine against one virus,” said Gustavo Palacios, PhD, Professor of Microbiology at the Icahn School of Medicine and VITAL project lead. “Rather than focusing only on which antigens are delivered, we want to understand which biological principles can be incorporated into vaccination so that the same framework can eventually be adapted across different respiratory threats. H5N1 gives us a rigorous starting point to test those principles.” The approach is built around five biological principles: ​​targeting exclusively the expression of the immunogen in immune cells that help activate the body’s immune response; providing appropriate stimulation to those cells; engineering antigens to reduce toxicity and adverse responses; matching antigen delivery to a pathogen’s natural route of entry; and ​​developing pulse immunization, a strategy designed to ​generate an immune response that ​mimic aspects of natural infection through controlled patterns of exposure. The program brings together complementary expertise in viral genomics, molecular virology, vaccine development, and human immunology from internationally renowned investigators, including Dr. Palacios, Adolfo García-Sastre, PhD, and Ana Fernandez-Sesma, PhD, all faculty members in the Department of Microbiology at the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai. A central component of VITAL is antigen detoxification: engineering viral antigens to reduce potential toxicity while preserving antigen expression and immunogenicity. The program will also investigate different intranasal immunization schedules, including repeated low-dose regimens designed to mimic aspects of the timing of natural infection. For Dr. García-Sastre, whose research has focused extensively on influenza virus biology, virus-host interactions, and vaccine development, VITAL provides an opportunity to explore new strategies for a longstanding challenge in influenza vaccination: generating long-lasting immune protection against a range of virus variants. “One of the central challenges in influenza vaccination is achieving protection that is broad and durable rather than narrowly focused on a single circulating influenza virus variant,” said Dr. García-Sastre, Irene and Dr. Arthur M. Fishberg Professor of Medicine and Director of the Global Health and Emerging Pathogens Institute at the Icahn School of Medicine. “VITAL gives us an opportunity to explore a different way of approaching that problem—by engineering not only the antigen, but also how, where, and over what time course the immune system encounters it.” To understand those responses in greater depth, VITAL will combine human immune tissue models and animal models with single-cell and spatial analysis, proteomics, and artificial intelligence and computational approaches. The research will examine how targeted antigen-presenting cells, such as macrophages and dendritic cells, respond to vaccination, interact with each other, and how those interactions contribute to downstream B and T cell responses. That component of the program aligns closely with Dr. Fernandez-Sesma’s research on virus-host interactions and immune responses in human systems, including work involving macrophages, dendritic cells, and human tonsil-based models. “A major strength of VITAL is the ability to study how vaccination shapes the immune response in physiologically relevant human systems,” said Dr. Fernandez-Sesma, Chair of the Department of Microbiology at the Icahn School of Medicine. “By looking closely at macrophages, dendritic cells, and other immune populations using primary human tissues, we can predict whether a vaccine generates the appropriate immune response in humans as an alternative to animal models.” If the initial principles are successfully validated, VITAL is structured to expand beyond H5N1. The program is designed to scale toward a multivalent strategy encompassing at least 20 respiratory viruses, creating a framework that can be evaluated across a broader range of respiratory threats. Preclinical studies will evaluate the durability and breadth of immune responses across multiple experimental systems, including young and aged mice and ferrets, in addition to the human primary systems mentioned above. Animal models remain necessary under the current regulatory framework to characterize integrated immune responses, safety, and protection in vivo. These studies provide a bridge to a future framework in which validated human organoid systems may be accepted by regulatory agencies for defined aspects of preclinical evaluation. ​​The program also includes regulatory planning and Investigational New Drug-enabling activities to support the potential clinical translation of selected vaccine candidates. The VITAL project agreement runs through August 28, 2031. Its comprehensive system includes seven hospitals, more than 400 outpatient practices, over 600 research and clinical laboratories, the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai, the Graduate School of Biomedical Sciences, and the Mount Sinai Phillips School of Nursing. Together, the Health System comprises approximately 48,000 employees, more than 9,000 physicians, and 8,600 nurses. As a leading learning health system, Mount Sinai combines clinical expertise with scientific discovery to improve patient care while training the next generation of health care and biomedical leaders. The Health System provides care across every stage of life, from prenatal care through geriatrics, while advancing personalized medicine through artificial intelligence, data science, and biomedical research. Mount Sinai is consistently recognized among the nation’s leading academic health systems for patient care, research, and education. The Mount Sinai Hospital is ranked No. 1 in New York by Newsweek and No. 5 on the magazine’s World’s Best Hospitals list. The Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai ranks No. 11 among U.S. medical schools and No. 1 among freestanding medical schools for National Institutes of Health funding, reflecting the strength of its scientific enterprise and leadership in biomedical research. Sadiq Mohsen Published 15 October 2026, 12:17 Link copiedShare Save Thousands of Adélie penguins live in Antarctica’s remote Danger Islands. Thousands of Adélie penguins and other seabirds were found dead in Antarctica’s remote Danger Islands in March 2024. Laboratory tests detected the bacterium responsible for avian cholera in 46 of 49 sampled animals. Researchers say the findings highlight the need to monitor multiple diseases affecting Antarctic wildlife, not only bird flu. Thousands of penguins found dead in Antarctica in 2024 were primarily victims of avian cholera rather than bird flu, according to a new study that has revealed an overlooked threat to wildlife in the remote region. In Proceedings of the Royal Society B: Biological Sciences, examined a mass mortality event involving Adélie penguins and other seabirds in the Danger Islands archipelago off the Antarctic Peninsula. The discovery surprised researchers who initially suspected highly pathogenic avian influenza, commonly known as H5N1 bird flu, because the virus had recently reached Antarctica and raised concerns about its impact on local wildlife. However, laboratory testing and examinations of the animals revealed that avian cholera was responsible for most of the investigated deaths. Thousands of penguins found dead Dead penguins discovered during the expedition. In March 2024, an international research expedition visited the Danger Islands, which are home to more than 1.2 million breeding pairs of Adélie penguins. Researchers encountered thousands of dead penguins across two islands, alongside carcasses belonging to other seabird species. The scale of the deaths prompted concerns about a possible outbreak of bird flu. The H5N1 virus had recently spread to Antarctica, and scientists were investigating whether it was responsible for the sudden loss of wildlife. Researchers collected samples from 49 carcasses for laboratory analysis. The results showed that DNA from Pasteurella multocida, the bacterium that causes avian cholera, was detected in 46 of the sampled animals. H5N1 was detected in only a few. The findings identified avian cholera as the cause of most of the deaths investigated, demonstrating the importance of considering other diseases even when a major known pathogen is circulating. What is avian cholera? Scientists investigate the cause of death. Avian cholera is a contagious bacterial disease that affects birds and can cause severe illness and sudden death. It is caused by Pasteurella multocida, a bacterium that can spread through contact with infected animals and contaminated environments. In dense breeding colonies, where large numbers of birds gather, outbreaks can have serious consequences. Despite its name, avian cholera is different from the cholera that affects humans. The disease can progress rapidly, with bacteria spreading through the bloodstream and affecting multiple organs. This can make outbreaks particularly damaging when many birds are living in close proximity. Researchers say the latest findings show that avian cholera deserves greater attention in studies of Antarctic wildlife mortality. A disease that may have circulated for decades Genetic analysis revealed that the bacterial strain involved in the outbreak was closely related to one identified in Antarctic seabirds more than two decades ago. The researchers also found genetic links with strains detected elsewhere in the Southern Ocean, including locations thousands of kilometers away. These similarities suggest that the disease may be more widely distributed in the region than previously recognised. The findings do not establish a continuous record of outbreaks over the entire period, but they provide evidence that avian cholera has been present in the wider Antarctic environment for many years. Lead author Matteo Iervolino and his colleagues highlighted the importance of continued wildlife-health surveillance, particularly in remote locations where disease outbreaks can go undetected or remain unexplained. Why bird flu was initially suspected The discovery of H5N1 in Antarctica had raised concerns among scientists about the vulnerability of seabirds and marine mammals to the virus. Because bird flu can cause substantial mortality in wildlife, researchers initially considered it a likely explanation for the penguin deaths. However, the new study demonstrates that the presence of one concerning pathogen does not mean it is responsible for every mass mortality event. Researchers stressed that a broad investigation of infectious diseases is necessary to determine what is killing wildlife, especially when several pathogens may be circulating in the same region. The study does not suggest that bird flu is harmless to Antarctic animals. Instead, it shows that other diseases can cause significant losses and should not be overlooked. Protecting Antarctica’s wildlife The findings underline the challenges of monitoring wildlife in one of the world’s most remote environments. Antarctica’s isolation makes it difficult to investigate animal deaths quickly, while large breeding colonies can make outbreaks particularly consequential. Researchers say sustained monitoring could help scientists identify the causes of future mortality events and better understand how infectious diseases affect seabirds. The latest research does not establish that avian cholera alone threatens the entire Adélie penguin population with extinction. However, it identifies the disease as an important cause of mortality that requires further investigation. For scientists, the discovery is a reminder that protecting Antarctic wildlife requires more than monitoring a single virus. Understanding the range of pathogens circulating in the region will be essential to assessing future risks to penguins and other seabirds. (CDC/NIAID via AP, File) 1Comment Share topics: Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza Reno-Sparks Nevada Department of Wildlife Nevada Department of Agriculture Public health Wild geese Dead bird reporting HPAI symptoms The Nevada Department of Wildlife (NDOW) in coordination with the Nevada Department of Agriculture, and Nevada Division of Public and Behavioral Health confirmed an outbreak of Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (HPAI) in multiple flocks of geese in the Reno/Sparks region. Officials say the public can help by identifying infected geese, notifying the proper officials and disposing geese safely to reduce transmission to other birds and species. HPAI is a highly contagious virus that can infect poultry, wild waterfowl, and in rare cases can infect livestock and humans. HPAI symptoms in birds include: Sneezing, coughing, eye & nasal discharge, swelling or fluid accumulating around one or both eyes. Abnormal position of head or neck, poor balance and coordination, and/or circling. A buildup of fluid in the bird’s legs and patchy redness of the skin. Diarrhea and green discoloration of the feces. Weakness, lethargy, depression. Sudden death. If the public encounters a dead goose, officials encourage them to do the following: Powered By 10 Duane Davis sentenced 40 years to life in prison for murder of Tupac Shakur Share Next Stay Notify the landowner responsible. For geese found on City or County Parks, contact them for removal. City of Reno Parks can be reached at (775) 334-2270; Washoe County Parks phone is (775) 828-6612. Dispose waterfowl on your own property by double bagging it and placing it in municipal waste. Be sure to wear gloves, an N95 mask, and eye protection. If you encounter a dead goose and have poultry, please change your clothes and shoes afterwards. If the public encounters a sick goose, they are encouraged to: Leave the goose alone and contact NDOW at (775) 688-1500 to report the location of the goose. If this is on your property, someone will contact you as soon as possible. Keep pets and children away. If you have domestic birds, especially backyard poultry officials say you should do the following: Keep poultry in secure enclosures away from wild birds and waterfowl. Wear dedicated clothing and footwear when caring for poultry. Clean and disinfect tools and equipment after use. Store poultry feed securely and avoid placing wild bird feeders near poultry areas. Watch for unusual behavior, signs of illness or unexpected deaths in your flock. Avoid touching or handling sick or dead wild birds. Use gloves and protective gear when necessary. Contact a veterinarian if birds appear sick and report high mortality rates among domestic poultry to the NDA at diseasereporting@agri.nv.gov. Officials say HPAI rarely spreads to livestock and humans. In wild waterfowl populations, it usually displays without any signs of illness and low mortality rates. It can cause mortality in some species of geese, raptors and game birds. Poultry are highly susceptible to HPAI and mortality rates may exceed 90%. When HPAI does spread to humans, symptoms may include fever, cough, sore throat, difficulty breathing, eye irritation, headaches, runny or stuffy nose, body aches, diarrhea and vomiting. Transmission to humans may occur from contact with infected or potentially infected animals, animal carcasses, or surfaces contaminated with animal excretions without using proper protective clothing and equipment. If you or your family have been exposed to a sick or dead bird and develop any of these symptoms, contact your healthcare provider and let them know about your animal exposure. Contact Economic Players EN FRANCAIS News Entrepreneurs LOGISTIC HUB Business environment Indicators Recent reforms Panorama Legal and administrative framework Sectors Agriculture Energy Finance - Banking Mining Training Telecom News Entrepreneurs LOGISTIC HUB Business environment Indicators Recent reforms Panorama Legal and administrative framework Sectors Agriculture Energy Finance - Banking Mining Training Telecom Seven West African Countries Adopt Three Regional Animal Health Strategies Agriculture Wednesday, 14 October 2026 15:29 (Togo First) - Ministers overseeing the livestock sector in seven West African countries adopted three regional strategies to combat transboundary animal diseases at an October 8 meeting in Lomé, Togo. The action plans run from 2026 to 2031 and focus on protecting donkeys, preventing foot-and-mouth disease and controlling highly pathogenic avian influenza. Improving Regional Coordination Developed by the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) Regional Animal Health Center (RAHC), the strategies aim to align national policies, strengthen disease surveillance and improve animal health data sharing. The measures include putting information systems into operation, aligning national regulations and improving coordination among disease surveillance networks. The goal is to detect outbreaks earlier and coordinate responses across countries, in line with the One Health approach, which addresses health risks affecting people, animals and the environment. Economic Impact of Animal Diseases Animal diseases also pose economic risks across the region, where livestock production supports rural livelihoods and food security. According to figures published by Togo First, the livestock subsector accounted for nearly 7% of Togo's GDP and more than 16% of agricultural GDP, with agriculture itself contributing about 40% of the country's GDP. Disease outbreaks can also disrupt livestock production. In March 2025, Togo reported H5N1 bird flu cases at three farms, affecting nearly 6,500 birds. Authorities responded by culling affected birds and restricting poultry movements. At the Lomé meeting, ministers also emphasized the need to strengthen vaccination programs, tighten controls on animal movements and increase participation by livestock farmers' organizations. In Togo, the measures are consistent with broader efforts to increase livestock productivity and make the sector more resilient. ENFORCING CONTRACTS (more info) Compared to some years ago when it was one of the lowest rankers under the Doing Business’ Enforcing Contracts indicator, Togo, leveraging many efforts to improve its business climate, was able to jump significantly on the index in the recent years... . CONTRACT EXECUTION (more info) Creation of special chambers of commerce for small debts • Creation of chambers of commerce at the Court of Appeal • Civil and commercial cases now handled by distinct clerks • Establishment of commercial courts in Lomé and Kara • Lawyers and bailiffs now have access to the FORSETI COMMERCIAL platform • A maximum period of 100 days was fixed to settle a commercial dispute . TRADING ACROSS BORDERS (more info) In comparison to previous years,Togo has significantly improved its ranking under the“Trading across borders” indicator by adopting multiple reforms that focus mainly on the digitization and reduction in delays, for import and export procedures related to import and export. In comparison to previous years, Togo has significantly improved its ranking on the “Trading across borders” index by adopting multiple reforms that focus mainly on the digitalization and reduction in delays, for import and export procedures related to import and export. CONSTRUCTION PERMIT (more info) After moving from the 133rd to 127th place under the 2020 Doing Business’ construction permit index, Togo intends to reiterate this feat in the coming edition of the global ranking. To this end, it has introduced this year multiple reforms. GETTING ELECTRICITY (more info) Over the past two years, Togo’s ranking under the Doing Business’ Getting electricity and water indicator has increased consistently. Owing this performance to multiple reforms aimed at making it easier for businesses to access power and water, Lomé plans to introduce even more reforms this year to keep up its improvements. REGISTERING A PROPERTY (more info) Out of all the 'Doing Business’ indicators, Property Registration is where Togo has improved the most since 2018. Indeed, after spending years in the lowest part of this ranking, the country now seeks to beat Rwanda which is the best performer on this index in Africa. To do so, Lomé has been introducing many reforms, with the latest batch implemented this year. PUBLIC PROCUREMENT (more info) From professionalization to digitization, through legislative regulations, Togo’s public procurement framework is constantly being modernized. Several reforms have been implemented to improve the sector much to the benefit of the private sector, which is the focus of the National Development Plan. PAYING TAXES AND DUTIES (more info) To improve its business environment, Togo introduced some important reforms related to the payment of tax and duties. From the replacement of some taxes to the cancellation of others through exemptions, the country has only one objective: offer the most attractive tax framework to investors and economic operators. It is increasingly a practical framework for protecting profitability, reducing resource losses and securing the future of animal protein production. ADM’s approach aligns with its Next Generation Thinking strategy, which focuses on helping customers improve resource efficiency, production performance, and environmental outcomes. For animal nutrition professionals, sustainability can be viewed through 3 connected pillars: economic, environmental and social sustainability. Economic sustainability is the foundation of resilient production systems. A farm, integrator or feed business must remain profitable to continue investing in better practices, new technologies and long-term improvement. Feed cost efficiency, lower mortality, fewer downgraded products, improved feed conversion and longer productive lifespans all contribute directly to that objective. Environmental sustainability focuses on producing animal protein while using fewer natural resources and reducing pressure on land, water, air and biodiversity. In feed, this means improving nutrient efficiency, reducing nitrogen, phosphorus and mineral excretion, limiting avoidable waste and responsible sourcing raw materials. ADM supports these efforts through traceability and responsible sourcing programs aligned with its ambition to develop deforestation – and conversion – free supply chains, particularly in areas identified as having a greater risk of deforestation and ecosystem conversion. Social sustainability completes the picture by supporting safe, transparent and responsible food systems. It includes animal welfare, food safety, responsible use of resources, and the long-term viability of the people, farms and communities involved across the agricultural value chain. Starting with economics: The SINCRO treasure hunt ADM’s SINCRO service offering is based on a clear principle: progress must be measurable. The journey therefore begins with economic sustainability. By analysing technical and economic results, SINCRO helps identify where value is being lost and where growth opportunities can be captured. This is especially relevant in an industry where small performance gaps can translate into significant financial impact at farm or feed mill level. This approach can be compared to a treasure hunt. In many production systems, hidden losses are present in the data: a slightly higher feed conversion ratio, marginally increased mortality, downgraded eggs, reduced animal longevity, or inconsistent raw material quality. Individually, these gaps may appear limited. When converted into economic value, however, they can reveal substantial sources of lost profit. ADM illustrates this logic through digital tools such as TreasurePerform, which helps convert technical gaps versus a reference into economic losses. A difference in feed conversion ratio, mortality, laying persistency or egg discard rate can be expressed in monetary terms, making priorities easier to discuss and decisions easier to make. This first diagnostic step creates the basis for targeted actions, combining services, expertise and solutions to improve technical performance and strengthen economic sustainability. From grain to farm: A holistic route to environmental sustainability Raw material sourcing has a major influence on the carbon footprint of animal feed. Using verified deforestation-free raw materials can reduce deforestation-related supply chain risk and may lower certain environmental impacts associated with feed ingredient sourcing, depending on the sourcing scenario and assessment methodology. ADM supports customers with traceable sourcing solutions and responsible supply chain programs designed to reduce risks linked to deforestation and conversion. Its soy strategy included traceability, supplier engagement, risk assessment and monitoring aimed at reducing deforestation and land-conversion risks within high-risk sourcing regions. As customers increasingly seek to quantify the environmental impact of feed ingredients, access to credible life cycle assessment (LCA) data has become an important component of responsible sourcing. ADM offers products supported by Global Feed LCA Institute (GFLI)-branded life cycle assessment data, including soybean meal and palm kernel expeller, enabling customers to make more informed sourcing decisions and support transparent environmental reporting. For palm kernel expeller, this verified data demonstrates up to a 25% lower carbon footprint compared with conventional alternatives, illustrating how ingredient selection can contribute to measurable emissions reductions across both the feed supply chain and livestock production. Precision nutrition is another practical lever for improving sustainability. It helps nutritionists formulate closer to animals’ real requirements while limiting excess nutrients and avoidable waste. This starts with accurate characterization of raw materials, including their quality and variability. Through SINCRO, ADM helps customers access laboratory analyses and NIR calibrations to support their quality control programs. ADM’s MatrixNutri app supports this approach by converting analytical results for more than 400 ingredients into precise, species-specific nutritional values, including values for aquaculture and providing a robust foundation for accurate feed formulation. Together, these services are designed to help reduce resource losses associated with formulation variability while supporting profitability thereby supporting both environmental and economic goals. A practical example can be seen in a broiler trial conducted by ADM in which crude protein in the finisher diet was reduced from 19% to 16.2% in parallel to specific adjustments. Final live weight was maintained, while total protein intake decreased. In this trial, modelling indicated that the carbon footprint of the finisher feed was up to 17% lower than the reference formulation. At farm gate, modelling indicated lower environmental impacts per kg of meat produced for the indicators assessed in the study. This illustrates how ADM’s nutrition expertise can help customers move beyond least-cost formulation toward a broader optimization model that integrates economic, zootechnical, and environmental objectives. ADM’s broad portfolio of feed additives and specialty solutions complements its grain-to-farm approach by helping customers reduce production losses and improve resource efficiency and farm performance. Improving eggshell quality, for example, can reduce the number of downgraded or discarded eggs. Supporting laying hen longevity can reduce the non-productive investment represented by replacement pullets. Improving sow robustness and reproductive performance can reduce culling and save resources. Organic trace mineral solutions, such as the B-Traxim range, can support mineralbioavailability, thereby contributing to lower mineral excretion. In this context, ADM’s Next Generation Thinking strategy is not positioned as an opposition between profitability and sustainability. Rather, it shows that both objectives can reinforce each other when data, nutrition expertise and field performance are connected. By reducing technical gaps, improving nutrient use and animal robustness, limiting waste and supporting responsible raw materials sourcing, animal feed professionals can create more efficient production systems that are economically robust and designed to use resources more efficiently and reduce production losses. Conclusion: Building sustainable value through measurable improvement For the animal feed industry, the most effective sustainability strategies are those that can be measured, implemented and translated into value. ADM’s approach starts with economic performance because profitability gives producers the capacity to invest, adapt and improve. From there, SINCRO connects control of raw materials, precision nutrition and performance monitoring to help reduce variability and unlock hidden opportunities. ADM feed additives and specialty solutions provide another practical lever, helping improve nutrient efficiency, animal robustness, product quality and loss reduction across species and production systems. Actions that improve farm profitability, such as better feed efficiency, fewer losses, stronger animal robustness, longer productive lifespans and more accurate formulation, can also lower the use of natural resources. Responsible sourcing and traceability help address environmental risks associated with key raw materials, including land-use change and deforestation, before those materials enter the feed mill. This holistic model shows that sustainability is not a separate agenda for animal nutrition, but an integrated process supported by ADM at each step of the value chain. By combining sourcing expertise, analytical tools, nutrition services, performance monitoring and tailored solutions, ADM can help customers build more competitive, transparent and resilient production systems for the future.Learn more about ADM’s SINCRO solutions here. Wildlife Biologists Start Vaccinating Shy Albatrosses by Hand, Taking Aim at the Spread of Avian Flu in Tasmania If all goes to plan, officials hope to vaccinate up to 100 of the large seabirds on Albatross Island, giving each two doses of the vaccine. Afterward, they plan to keep tabs on the birds using remote cameras and follow-up visits Sarah Kuta | Daily Correspondent October 15, 2026 11:21 a.m. Share Copy linkEmailSMSFacebookXRedditLinkedInBlueskyPrint Add as preferred source Biologists are running a pilot project with up to 100 birds on Albatross Island. Department of Natural Resources and Environment Tasmania Wildlife officials in Australia are taking a hands-on approach to combating the deadly and highly contagious bird flu strain H5N1. Veterinarians and biologists have just begun a multi-week pilot project to capture and vaccinate shy albatrosses on a remote Tasmanian island. So far, the albatrosses have remained healthy and free from the virus. However, the avian flu recently reached Tasmania for the first time, and it has sickened dozens of birds from other species since then. Wildlife experts consider the shy albatross highly vulnerable to the H5N1 strain, so they’re taking steps to protect them. Officials hope the results of the pilot project will inform their broader efforts to combat the avian influenza “at a population level” in the species, Sheryl Hamilton, a wildlife biologist with Tasmania’s Department of Natural Resources and Environment, tells Kelsey Reid of the Australian Broadcasting Corporation (ABC). Officials hope the pilot project will inform their broader approach to vaccinating the birds. Department of Natural Resources and Environment Tasmania The shy albatross is a large seabird that breeds on three islets in the Bass Strait between the Australian mainland and the island state of Tasmania: Albatross Island, Mewstone and Pedra Branca. They’re considered “near threatened” by the International Union for Conservation of Nature and “vulnerable” in Tasmania. The total population includes an estimated 15,000 breeding pairs. If all goes to plan, officials hope to vaccinate up to 100 shy albatrosses on Albatross Island, giving each bird two doses of the vaccine. Afterward, they plan to keep an eye on the birds using remote cameras and follow-up visits to see how they respond. The process is labor-intensive. Wearing head-to-toe hazmat suits, wildlife biologists pick up each bird by hand, weigh it and administer the first dose of the vaccine. They then mark the birds with temporary, nontoxic paint and place numbered markers at their nests to keep track of which individuals are part of the project. They plan to return in a few weeks to administer the second dose. Vaccinating wild birds is difficult because they’re hard to catch and constantly on the move, making it challenging to recapture them for a second dose. However, shy albatrosses provide a “unique opportunity,” since they can be safely approached multiple times while nesting and monitored “in a way that’s not possible for many wild species,” Guy Barnett, the Tasmanian minister for environment and climate change, says in a statement. Veterinarians have also been vaccinating little penguins against the bird flu on Phillip Island and St Kilda beach in Victoria, Australia. The squat, black-and-white birds don’t fly, and they return to the same spot each night, making them relatively easy to catch for both doses. So far, more than 1,500 birds have received their first dose. Did you know? Airlifting nests In 2017, biologists airlifted artificial shy albatross nests to Albatross Island in a bid to boost the species’ breeding success. Warmer and wetter weather, driven by climate change, had been making it harder for the birds’ natural nests to stay together, biologists said. Tasmania recorded its first official case of the bird flu in August, when a brown skua found on the island’s northwest coast tested positive. Since then, the number of bird flu “events”—in which the virus is detected in one or more animals—has risen to 50, with a Pacific gull, a great crested tern, a little penguin and a black currawong among the latest species affected by the virus, reports Olivia Hicks for 7BU. The virus has not been detected in commercial poultry or backyard flocks, and Tasmania has not experienced any mass mortality events. Australia had been the only continent without avian influenza until June, when the virus was detected in wild seabirds in the state of Western Australia. Since then, the bird flu has sickened a variety of seabirds and mammals on the continent and its surrounding islands, from greater ‌crested terns to long-nosed fur seals. The virus has also been detected in endangered Australian sea lions and urban foxes. So far, the virus has not been detected in shy albatrosses. Department of Natural Resources and Environment Tasmania Across Australia, officials have recorded 706 total bird flu events at last count. Officials are concerned about the spread of the virus in Australia and New Zealand, which are home to many vulnerable species found nowhere else on Earth. The situation is “quite frightening,” Rachael Gray, a veterinary pathologist at the University of Sydney, tells ABC’s Jacinta Bowler and Peter de Kruijff. “It’s pretty overwhelming at the moment,” she adds. “These animals, who we very much love and admire and respect ... these animals are getting sick, they are suffering and then they are dying.” You Might Also Like Birds in Their Pants: Two Men Accused of Smuggling 21 Avians After Miami Airport Bust October 15, 2026 Construction Work on the North Dakota Governor's Residence Accidentally Unearthed Seven Coffins Dating Back to the State's Early Settlement October 15, 2026 China Has an Ancient Tradition of Building Beautiful Paper Kites October 15, 2026 See the Stunning Winners of the Wildlife Photographer of the Year Contest, Capturing the Splendor and Drama of Nature October 14, 2026 A New Contender for the World's Oldest Shipwreck Has Been Discovered Off the Coast of Turkey. supplementary_news.content: 24/7 LiveLos AngelesOrange CountyInland EmpireVentura CountyCalifornia 87° Bald Eagle Big Bear bald eagle Jackie's cause of death revealed in new necropsy report Big Bear's beloved bald eagle Jackie died from complications related to highly pathogenic avian influenza, according to necropsy results. KABC Thursday, October 15, 2026 3:58PM Share BIG BEAR, Calif. (KABC) -- Big Bear's beloved bald eagle Jackie died from complications related to a type of infectious avian flu, according to necropsy results. The California Department of Fish and Wildlife, San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance and Ojai Raptor Center on Wednesday released the results of testing conducted after Jackie's death, shedding new light on the illness that veterinarians had been trying to diagnose during weeks of treatment. The findings determined that highly pathogenic avian influenza, or bird flu, was the primary underlying cause of Jackie's decline. "Jackie's necropsy confirmed Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (HPAI) as the primary underlying cause of her decline," said Steve Kubiski, director of disease investigations for the San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance. "In an uncommon presentation of the virus, the infection caused a severe ulcer in her stomach that led to persistent internal bleeding, anemia, and the development of bacterial sepsis." The damage also allowed bacteria to enter her body, resulting in a serious secondary infection. Additional testing found evidence of the virus in multiple tissues. The results help explain the severe anemia that veterinarians were battling while caring for Jackie at the Ojai Raptor Center earlier this year. Jackie spent more than three weeks receiving intensive treatment, including oxygen therapy and a life-saving blood transfusion, as experts worked to determine what was making her sick. Toxicology testing detected brodifacoum, a rodent poison, in Jackie's liver. However, officials said the findings did not show the type of uncontrolled bleeding associated with the poison, and it was not identified as the primary cause of her illness or death. "The necropsy results have helped connect many of the findings we were seeing throughout the eagle's hospitalization," said Chris Eksteen, executive director of Ojai Raptor Center. "We are grateful to the many veterinary specialists, laboratories, wildlife agencies and partner organizations who worked alongside our team to understand her illness and provide her with the best possible care. Caring for her was an extraordinary privilege for our entire team." Big Bear's beloved bald eagle Jackie, who had been receiving intensive medical care for a prolonged illness, has died. See the timeline of her rescue and treatment here. Jackie died Aug. 10 after her condition continued to deteriorate despite treatment. Her remains were later cremated by the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service's National Eagle Repository, according to wildlife officials. "The story of the Big Bear bald eagle reflects the powerful connection people feel to these iconic birds," said CDFW Director Meghan Hertel. "We're grateful to everyone who cared for her and worked to support her well-being. Understanding the results of these tests is an important part of learning from this case and can help inform the care and treatment of other eagles and wildlife in the future." Jackie's death marked the loss of one half of the iconic bald eagle pair that had occupied Big Bear Valley for years. Her mate, Shadow, remains in the area, and officials said there is no evidence that he or the pair's eaglets became sick. Jackie gained a worldwide following through the Friends of Big Bear Valley eagle camera, with millions of viewers tuning in over the years to watch her and Shadow raise their young. Wildlife officials said her story helped bring attention to bald eagles, conservation and the habitats they depend on. Read Full Bio Dean Fioresi Updated on: October 14, 2026 / 9:56 PM PDT / CBS LA Add CBS News on Google Big Bear bald eagle Jackie's cause of death has been revealed nearly two months after she died in August, following weeks of testing and rehabilitation. According to the California Department of Fish and Wildlife, a necropsy and additional testing determined that Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza, or HPAI, was the "primary underlying cause of her decline." "In an uncommon presentation of the virus, the infection caused a severe ulcer in her stomach that led to persistent internal bleeding, anemia, and the development of bacterial sepsis," said Steve Kubiski, the Director of Disease Investigations with the San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance, which performed the necropsy. Jackie, who was estimated to be around 14 years old, died nearly a month after she was rescued from the Big Bear Lake shoreline, where she was found after being seen in a fight with two subadult eagles in July. Jackie, the Big Bear bald eagle who captured the awe of millions over the years via the Big Bear Bald Eagle Nest Cam. Friends of Big Bear Valley A team of veterinary experts at the Ojai Raptor Center oversaw her care in the weeks that followed, documenting the process as they tried to nurse her back to health. Despite undergoing a blood transfusion, which briefly provided a glimpse of hope, Jackie continued to suffer setbacks in her recovery due to the sickness, which remained a mystery until Wednesday's announcement by California wildlife officials. "Jackie showed signs of chronic disease involving the ventriculus, the muscular portion of a bird's stomach, commonly called the gizzard. The damaged and ulcerated tissue contributed to ongoing blood loss and her persistent severe anemia," the CDFW release said. "It also allowed bacteria to enter the body, resulting in a serious secondary bacterial infection." Officials said that additional testing also revealed severe inflammation and blood clot formation in Jackie's heart and several major blood vessels, and that the HPAI virus genetic material was present in several tissues throughout her body, including the ulcerated tissue in her ventriculus. Other tests showed Jackie was negative for West Nile Virus, and heavy metal levels were within acceptable limits. While toxicology screening detected brodifacoum, an anticoagulant rodenticide, in Jackie's liver, the necropsy did not find uncontrolled bleeding typically associated with the chemical pesticide, so it was not identified as her primary cause of illness or death. "Together, the findings showed that Jackie was suffering from multiple severe and interconnected disease processes that had been developing over time and ultimately led to her decline and death," CDFW's release said. Jackie and Shadow in 2024. Friends of Big Bear Valley Jackie's remains were cremated by the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service's National Eagle Repository, following the established procedures intended to prevent the transmission of HPAI to wildlife or humans, the release said. "The story of the Big Bear bald eagle reflects the powerful connection people feel to these iconic birds," said a statement from CDFW Director Meghan Hertel. "We're grateful to everyone who cared for her and worked to support her well-being. Understanding the results of these tests is an important part of learning from this case and can help inform the care and treatment of other eagles and wildlife in the future." Jackie was an iconic fixture in Southern California, drawing the attention of millions across the United States thanks to the 24/7 livestream camera documenting her life and that of her partner, Shadow, from above Big Bear Lake. Over the years, the duo parented several clutches of eaglets, most recently Sandy and Luna. CDFW officials said that based on camera data, they have no evidence to suggest that Shadow or the eaglets were sick. "Jackie's story brought unprecedented public attention to bald eagles and the importance of protecting the habitats they depend on," the release from CDFW said. "Her life and the public's connection to her highlights the powerful role that wildlife can play in connecting people to conservation." In the weeks since her death, Jackie has been honored with a massive memorial service in Big Bear, a life-size monument at a park in the San Bernardino Mountains and an Ontario Tower Buzzers minor league baseball game dedicated to celebrating her life. California state legislators also passed a resolution in her honor, proclaiming September 4 as California Wildlife Day. Facebook Linkedin Threads Whatsapp Reddit Email Page link A recent study has proposed a road map for countries to better monitor wildlife health and disease outbreaks. Previous research found that nearly 60% of the 107 countries it surveyed showed no evidence of a functional wildlife health surveillance system. This leaves ecosystems, agriculture, and human populations vulnerable to catastrophic outbreaks, the researchers say. The blueprint presented in the latest study offers actionable solutions to improve surveillance, said study co-author Sarah Olson, director of health at the Wildlife Conservation Society (WCS). “Earlier research did a good job diagnosing the problem in terms of what’s missing, and what wildlife health surveillance needs to deliver,” Olson told Mongabay by email. “This paper goes further: it uses a Theory of Change to map out how we actually close that gap, given limited resources and fragmented networks, to reach real collaborative surveillance. The challenge now is scaling efforts and expertise through a global community of practice — no single organization can meet this need alone, and the more we collaborate, the faster surveillance can grow everywhere.” Olson and her colleagues write that unmonitored disease events have already inflicted severe ecological and economic damage; for instance, sheep and goat plague caused an estimated 80% decline in Mongolia’s endangered saiga antelope (Saiga tatarica), while highly pathogenic avian influenza (H5N1) continues to trigger mass mortality across populations of wild birds and marine mammals. Mongabay recently reported on the spread of H5N1 affecting wild birds, urban wildlife, and live animal markets across cities like New York. The researchers say that if lethal pathogens can spread unchecked in heavily monitored megacities, the risks are vastly magnified in regions lacking basic biosurveillance. However, existing monitoring efforts remain plagued by sporadic, crisis-driven funding that evaporates as soon as emergencies subside, according to the researchers. To overcome these systemic barriers, the study outlines a collaborative road map or “theory of change” designed by the Wildlife Health Intelligence Network (WHIN) to establish lasting, locally led surveillance programs. The road map identifies six pathways. This includes shifting mindsets away from viewing wildlife merely as an economic liability; securing dedicated political support and funding; and adopting evidence-based practices. A fourth pathway includes deploying user-driven tools like the shared HAWK data platform, a service for managing wildlife health surveillance data. The other steps include strengthening frontline workforce skills, and mobilizing a global community of practice. Rather than imposing top-down mandates, the road map advocates scaling up proven regional models, such as WildHealthNet in Southeast Asia, to integrate community monitoring directly into national legislation. The authors noted that many of the recognized experts in this field are in high-income countries, creating a significant limitation in global representation. But Olson said the network is intentionally structured to reverse that imbalance, “by elevating local expertise from low- and middle-income countries along with Indigenous-led and community-led efforts.” Banner image: Dead elephant seal pups on a beach in Argentine Patagonia. Jackie, the beloved California bald eagle whose life was watched via live video feeds by millions around the world, died of complications resulting from avian influenza, according to a newly released necropsy report. "Jackie's necropsy confirmed Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (HPAI) as the primary underlying cause of her decline," Steve Kubiski, director of disease investigations for the San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance, said in a statement Wednesday, Oct. 14. "In an uncommon presentation of the virus, the infection caused a severe ulcer in her stomach that led to persistent internal bleeding, anemia, and the development of bacterial sepsis." The newly released report sheds light on the mysterious illness that veterinarians struggled to treat throughout the summer. The Big Bear Lake, California, bald eagle's life was livestreamed on YouTube, leading to her becoming an object of global fascination and to her hometown becoming practically synonymous with America's iconic bird. She died in August after a weeks-long fight with an illness that confounded the eagle's doctors. Efforts to save Jackie saw her hospitalized and placed under anesthesia for veterinarians to perform what many hoped would be a life-saving blood transfusion. Veterinary pathologists at the San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance performed the necropsy. According to the report released by the California Department of Fish and Wildlife, the avian flu left Jackie with a severe stomach ulcer that led to ongoing blood loss and ultimately a deadly bacterial infection. "Together, the findings showed that Jackie was suffering from multiple severe and interconnected disease processes that had been developing over time and ultimately led to her decline and death," the California Department of Fish and Wildlife said of the report. The state agency said that HPAI is a highly infectious disease that has been circulating in wild bird populations throughout the United States. Eagles and other raptors are believed to contract the disease through contact with infected birds or by eating infected prey. Waterfowl and shorebirds are natural carriers of the viruses. Jackie was hatched in 2012, the first eaglet to do so in Big Bear Valley, USA TODAY previously reported. Her parents, Ricky and Lucy, became the first known adult eagles who decided to stay in Big Bear Valley, which until then had only been a part-time winter destination for the species. Big Bear Lake is about an hour northeast of San Bernardino in Southern California. She lived in Big Bear Valley in the San Bernardino National Forest. She became a viral sensation a few years later when U.S. Forest Service employee Sandy Steers got the idea to install a webcam 120 feet off the forest floor to broadcast her life. Jackie found her first romance in 2017 when she mated with an eagle named Mr. B. The couple's eggs hatched in 2018, and while one of the eaglets died after a 24-hour rainstorm, the other, named Stormy, survived and left Big Bear that summer. Her second mate, Shadow, remains in Big Bear, state authorities said. California wildlife officials said that there is nothing to indicate he or their eaglets, Sandy and Luna, are sick. "The story of the Big Bear bald eagle reflects the powerful connection people feel to these iconic birds," said wildlife agency Director Meghan Hertel. "We’re grateful to everyone who cared for her and worked to support her well-being. Understanding the results of these tests is an important part of learning from this case and can help inform the care and treatment of other eagles and wildlife in the future." supplementary_news.content: Yona Tugg and colleagues show that a polyclonal secretory immunoglobulin A preparation, purified from breast milk pooled from multiple donors, neutralized respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), human adenovirus type 5, and H1N1 and H3N2 influenza A viruses in laboratory assays. In mouse models of H1N1 influenza infection, two intranasal doses of LCTG-001, given two hours before and 24 hours after infection, reduced illness and lung damage in both immunocompetent and antibody-deficient mice. In immunocompetent mice, lung viral loads were lower early in infection but comparable to controls later, despite less lung damage and better lung barrier integrity. The findings support further study of mucosal passive immunization for individuals with antibody deficiencies, although efficacy in humans has not been established. LCTG-001 could also be a candidate for seasonal influenza prevention and pandemic response, the researchers suggest. Tugg et al. produced the purified IgA product from breast milk collected from 120 donors through milk banks in Indianapolis and Pittsburgh. LCTG-001 also bound proteins and virus-like particles from H5N1 avian influenza viruses in clade 2.3.4.4b, but showed little neutralizing activity against the H5N1 strain tested; protection against H5N1 was not tested in animals. In laboratory assays, LCTG-001 inhibited influenza neuraminidase activity and stimulated human neutrophils when complexed with influenza antigens; the contribution of these activities to protection in mice remains unresolved. Source: Journal reference: Tugg, Y., et al. (2026). Polyclonal breast milk–derived secretory IgA confers broad antiviral protection against multiple respiratory viruses. Science Advances. supplementary_news.content: News Health Breast milk antibodies reduced lung damage in mice — News-Medical UA.NEWS 15 October 2026 05:53 In the United States, the breast milk antibody preparation LCTG-001 reduced disease manifestations and lung damage in mice infected with the H1N1 influenza virus. The study used purified polyclonal secretory immunoglobulin A obtained from pooled breast milk from donors. Results of experiments in mice As News-Medical reports , the animals received two intranasal doses of the preparation: two hours before infection and 24 hours afterward. The effect was recorded both in mice with normal immune systems and in animals with antibody deficiency. In mice with normal immune systems, the amount of virus in the lungs was lower than in the control group at the early stage of infection. Later, the viral load became comparable to that in the control group; however, animals that received the preparation had less lung damage and better lung barrier function. More current news is available on the UA.News Telegram channel Telegram . Activity against several viruses In laboratory tests, LCTG-001 neutralized respiratory syncytial virus, human adenovirus type 5, and influenza A viruses of the H1N1 and H3N2 subtypes. The preparation also inhibited influenza virus neuraminidase activity and stimulated human neutrophils when it formed complexes with influenza antigens. At the same time, researchers have not yet established the role of these mechanisms in protecting mice. Breast milk from 120 donors, collected through milk banks in Indianapolis and Pittsburgh in the United States, was used to produce LCTG-001. The preparation bound to proteins and virus-like particles of H5N1 avian influenza clade 2.3.4.4b, but showed little neutralizing activity against the tested H5N1 strain. Its protective effect against this virus was not tested in animals. The researchers note that the results justify further study of passive mucosal immunization for people with antibody deficiencies. The effectiveness of LCTG-001 in humans has not yet been established. Read us on Download our app

supplementary_news.content_title: 荷兰室内与可户外进入肉鸡生产系统中高致病性禽流感(HPAI)相关生物安全实施差异的横断面比较研究 - 生物通
supplementary_news.content: 荷兰室内与可户外进入肉鸡生产系统中高致病性禽流感(HPAI)相关生物安全实施差异的横断面比较研究 《Poultry Science》:Biosecurity implementation in indoor and outdoor-access broiler production systems in the Netherlands 【字体: 大 中 小 】 时间:2026年10月14日 来源:Poultry Science 4.5 为了促进科学的传播,生物通采集了这篇文章 订阅BioHot点这里解锁原文链接推送! “畅读会员”点此登录查看原文链接 Open access 家禽养殖场良好的生物安全实践可改善动物健康、福利和生产性能,但不同养殖场间的实施差异很大。反复发生的高致病性禽流感(HPAI)暴发以及具有户外通道的更高福利系统的扩张,引发了对暴露风险可能存在差异的担忧。然而,生物安全实施在不同生产系统间的差异程度仍不清楚。研究人员开展了一项横断面比较研究,以评估荷兰肉鸡养殖场中与HPAI相关的生物安全实践和风险因素,比较集约化系统(仅室内)和粗放化系统(生长较慢的肉鸡并具有带顶棚户外通道)。该研究纳入78个养殖场(63个集约化和15个粗放化)。生物安全使用Biocheck.UGent调查的统一化子集进行评估。从40个可比变量中,根据与HPAI引入和传播途径的相关性选择28个变量。采用带马蹄形先验(horseshoe priors)的贝叶斯逻辑回归(Bayesian logistic regression)评估生产系统间差异。大多数生物安全措施在系统间没有显著差异,在集约化和粗放化养殖场内均观察到相当大的变异。估计差异最大的是尸体储存清洁、饲养密度和雏鸡运送频率,尽管这些差异的统计学支持程度不一。饲养密度和运送频率反映系统间的结构性差异,而尸体储存清洁反映管理实践差异。这些发现表明,针对养殖场特定薄弱环节、辅以量身定制生物安全计划和现场指导的干预措施,可能比仅基于系统的建议更有效。 论文解读:荷兰室内与可户外进入肉鸡生产系统中高致病性禽流感相关生物安全实施比较 欢迎领取《放射性同位素检测一站式解决方案》 领 取 研究背景与问题:高致病性禽流感(highly pathogenic avian influenza, HPAI)持续威胁家禽业,暴发造成经济损失并引发公共卫生担忧。荷兰家禽养殖场密度高且水域丰富、吸引迁徙和居留水鸟,反复发生HPAI传入,导致大规模扑杀和移动限制。欧洲养禽业因农场集中、动物和车辆移动频繁、野鸟水禽沿主要飞行路线暴露而脆弱。近期HPAI季节影响欧盟包括荷兰的室内和户外生产系统。肉鸡生产在欧洲分为集约化和粗放化:集约化通常使用快速生长品种,生产周期35至42天,饲养密度可达或超过33 kg/m2;粗放化使用慢速生长品种,周期56至81天,密度较低,常提供户外通道。这些结构差异可能以不同方式影响暴露途径。生物安全(biosecurity)是降低HPAI传入及农场内和农场间传播的主要手段,包括外部生物安全(防止病原进入)和内部生物安全(限制进入后传播)。关键传入途径包括污染车辆和设备、人员移动、直接或间接接触野鸟。但生物安全实施和依从性在农场间差异很大。当前研究主要关注常规系统,对生产系统与生物安全要求和HPAI风险关联的评估有限,且“集约化”和“粗放化”定义不一致限制跨研究比较。使用统一化、与HPAI相关措施直接比较集约化和粗放化肉鸡系统的研究很少。荷兰同时存在常规仅室内肉鸡生产和慢速生长肉鸡加户外通道的替代概念,因此可在同一国家法规背景下比较。研究人员假设,虽然系统水平结构特征不同,但各系统内农场间生物安全实践仍存在显著变异。 关键技术方法:研究人员开展横断面比较研究(cross-sectional comparative study),纳入78个荷兰肉鸡养殖场。63个集约化农场来自Biocheck.UGent数据库(2015至2023年调查),15个粗放化农场于2023年12月至2024年5月通过专业网络招募并现场访问。使用Biocheck.UGent调查的统一化子集,将两版问卷协调后保留40个可比变量,并依据与HPAI传入和传播途径的相关性选择28个变量。主要统计方法为带正则化马蹄形先验(regularized horseshoe prior)的贝叶斯逻辑回归(Bayesian logistic regression),以生产系统为二分类结局;同时进行描述统计、最小-最大归一化热图、时间、先验和模型敏感性分析,以及Pareto平滑重要性抽样留一法交叉验证(Pareto-smoothed importance-sampling leave-one-out, PSIS-LOO)和近似受试者工作特征曲线下面积(area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, AUC)。 研究结果: 在78个养殖场中比较生物安全(63个集约化,15个粗放化)。通过横断面调查与统一化Biocheck.UGent变量比较,未显示系统间清楚分离。 集约化与粗放化养殖场未分离成不同组,且未出现一致的系统水平模式。热图显示,集约化农场36个分类变量均有多于1个反应类别,粗放化农场34/36如此;粗放化农场仅有饲养密度和清空禽舍步骤数无变异。若干变量在两系统均呈持续高风险:饲料筒仓清洁与消毒、饲料运送频率、访客无禽期要求、与静水或流水邻近。其中水邻近和饲料运送频率反映固定环境或结构特征,其余与农场管理实践相关。 在28个变量中,绝对后验均值系数最大的3个分类变量为尸体储存清洁、饲养密度和雏鸡运送频率。贝叶斯模型以集约化=0、粗放化=1编码生产系统,系数描述控制其他变量后各反应类别与生产系统的关联,不是因果效应;负系数表示与集约化农场关联,正系数表示与粗放化农场关联。尸体储存清洁方面,以“总是”清洁为参考,“有时”清洁后验均值系数为–2.38(95%可信区间[credible interval, CrI] –6.28至0.06;负系数后验概率0.93),提示该反应更常见于集约化农场,但95% CrI包括零;“从不”和“无独立尸体储存”接近零且区间宽。描述结果显示,61.9%(39/63)集约化农场报告“有时”清洁,粗放化农场为0/15;60.0%(9/15)粗放化农场报告“总是”清洁。饲养密度以“不超过33 kg/m2”为参考,超过33 kg/m2的后验均值系数为–3.22(95% CrI –7.05至0.02;负系数后验概率0.96),提示高密度在粗放化农场较少见,但95% CrI包括零;所有粗放化农场(15/15)密度不超过33 kg/m2,71.4%(45/63)集约化农场超过该阈值。雏鸡运送频率以“少于3次”为参考,“3至6次”后验均值系数为+1.08(95% CrI –0.22至4.59;正系数后验概率0.80),提示粗放化农场更常处于中等频率,但方向支持较弱且95% CrI包括零;“超过6次”接近零。描述结果显示,93.3%(14/15)粗放化农场每年3至6次,65.1%(41/63)集约化农场超过6次。其余23个分类变量和雇佣人数后验均值接近零但可信区间宽,不能解释为系统间相似;经理经验每年系数较小(后验均值–0.05,95% CrI –0.14至0.01;负系数后验概率0.94)。近似PSIS-LOO交叉验证AUC为0.94,反映该数据集内农场分离而非可推广预测性能。 时间敏感性分析显示集约化农场总体模式大致稳定,但若干变量在时期之间有描述性变化,尤其饲养密度、分多步清空禽舍、装卸区清洁消毒和经理经验。超过33 kg/m2比例从2022年前78.7%(37/47)降至之后50.0%(8/16)。由于所有粗放化农场均在2022年后调查,模型无法完全分离时间和系统差异;将调查时期作为协变量后,超过33 kg/m2系数从–3.22减弱至–1.31,而尸体储存清洁关联仍一致(调整前后–2.38和–2.82)。先验和模型敏感性分析对该3个变量估计大致相似;排除结构性系统关联变量后尸体储存清洁关联仍一致。 讨论部分总结与结论翻译: 讨论指出,本研究旨在识别荷兰肉鸡农场生物安全实施变异,并评估其是否系统性与生产系统相关。通过统一化Biocheck.UGent子集比较28个HPAI相关措施,发现有限证据支持生产系统间系统性差异,两组内均有显著变异。最大估计差异涉及尸体储存清洁消毒、饲养密度和雏鸡运送频率,但统计支持不一。近零系数不能因整体变异小解释;观察到的变异似乎分布在个体农场而非与生产系统一致,但仅15个粗放化农场且变量多,估计不精确,宽可信区间不能排除中等系统差异。若干措施在两系统均持续高风险,提示行业共同薄弱环节,包括饲料筒仓清洁、访客无禽期等,改善实施不太可能仅依赖意识。尸体储存清洁是唯一直接可修改管理实践且敏感性分析最一致;但尸体储存配置理解可能影响回答,荷兰家禽产业链质量方案(IKB Kip)允许尸体储存整合于禽舍而非物理独立设施。饲养密度是明确结构差异,绝大多数集约化超过33 kg/m2,粗放化无一超过,符合欧盟定义;不应视为生物安全差或HPAI传入风险高,且不等于农场或群体规模。2003年荷兰H 7 N 7 疫情中较大农场规模与HPAI传入相关,而饲养类型无关;近期模型显示较小农场规模降低模拟HPAI流行规模,但未完全抵消户外农场增加带来的传入风险和流行规模增加。雏鸡运送频率对比更弱,反映生产周期长度;欧洲食品安全局(EFSA)评估欧盟内活禽包括一日龄雏鸡移动导致HPAI传入可能性为不太可能。频繁雏鸡运送本身不应解释为更高HPAI传入风险,还取决于接触周围生物安全措施;集约化农场更常报告雏鸡运输车辆装车前清洁消毒(61/63对8/15),但该变量未纳入模型。实践意义是生产系统单独为生物安全实施的有限代理,干预应针对农场特定薄弱环节;Biocheck.UGent可用于基准评估和识别改进领域,兽医指导可改善家禽农场生物安全评分。政策应补充系统级法规与农场级实施支持,行业组织在雏鸡运送物流、饲料运输和尸体收集等需协调措施中有作用。同时,一般生物安全措施相似实施不代表系统间HPAI暴露相同,户外通道可能增加直接或间接接触野鸟和污染环境的机会,这种系统特定暴露未被统一化措施捕获。局限包括观察与自报混合、非随机抽样、集约化样本来自便利样本且可能偏向更高生物安全意识、粗放化农场数少、时间差异、横断面设计、残余混杂、排除系统特定问题以及风险评分未与HPAI发病率关联。 研究结论翻译:总之,大多数与HPAI相关的生物安全措施在集约化和粗放化肉鸡农场之间呈现重叠的反应分布,每个系统内农场间存在显著变异。在最大对比中,尸体储存清洁是唯一直接可修改的实践,并且在敏感性分析中最一致,而饲养密度和雏鸡运送频率主要反映系统的结构性特征。这些发现表明,仅生产系统不能充分反映实践中的生物安全表现。因此,生物安全改进应同时针对农场特定薄弱环节和整个行业共同的实施缺口。同时,一般生物安全措施的相似实施并不能消除系统特定暴露途径,特别是与户外通道相关的暴露途径。未来研究应在更大规模和纵向研究中验证这些发现,纳入系统特定暴露途径(如户外系统中野生鸟类接触),评估农场定制生物安全干预和现场指导是否能带来可测量的实施与疾病预防改善,并确定此处发现的共同薄弱环节是否也存在于其他国家和生产系统。 论文解读:荷兰室内与可户外进入肉鸡生产系统中高致病性禽流感相关生物安全实施比较研究背景与问题:高致病性禽流感(highly pathogenic avian influenza, HPAI)持续威胁家禽业,暴发造成经济损失并引发公共卫生担忧。荷兰家禽养殖场密度高且水域丰富、吸引迁徙和居留水鸟,反复发生HPAI传入,导致大规模扑杀和移动限制。欧洲养禽业因农场集中、动物和车辆移动频繁、野鸟水禽沿主要飞行路线暴露而脆弱。近期HPAI季节影响欧盟包括荷兰的室内和户外生产系统。肉鸡生产在欧洲分为集约化和粗放化:集约化通常使用快速生长品种,生产周期35至42天,饲养密度可达或超过33 kg/m;粗放化使用慢速生长品种,周期56至81天,密度较低,常提供户外通道。这些结构差异可能以不同方式影响暴露途径。生物安全(biosecurity)是降低HPAI传入及农场内和农场间传播的主要手段,包括外部生物安全(防止病原进入)和内部生物安全(限制进入后传播)。关键传入途径包括污染车辆和设备、人员移动、直接或间接接触野鸟。但生物安全实施和依从性在农场间差异很大。当前研究主要关注常规系统,对生产系统与生物安全要求和HPAI风险关联的评估有限,且“集约化”和“粗放化”定义不一致限制跨研究比较。使用统一化、与HPAI相关措施直接比较集约化和粗放化肉鸡系统的研究很少。荷兰同时存在常规仅室内肉鸡生产和慢速生长肉鸡加户外通道的替代概念,因此可在同一国家法规背景下比较。研究人员假设,虽然系统水平结构特征不同,但各系统内农场间生物安全实践仍存在显著变异。关键技术方法:研究人员开展横断面比较研究(cross-sectional comparative study),纳入78个荷兰肉鸡养殖场。63个集约化农场来自Biocheck.UGent数据库(2015至2023年调查),15个粗放化农场于2023年12月至2024年5月通过专业网络招募并现场访问。使用Biocheck.UGent调查的统一化子集,将两版问卷协调后保留40个可比变量,并依据与HPAI传入和传播途径的相关性选择28个变量。主要统计方法为带正则化马蹄形先验(regularized horseshoe prior)的贝叶斯逻辑回归(Bayesian logistic regression),以生产系统为二分类结局;同时进行描述统计、最小-最大归一化热图、时间、先验和模型敏感性分析,以及Pareto平滑重要性抽样留一法交叉验证(Pareto-smoothed importance-sampling leave-one-out, PSIS-LOO)和近似受试者工作特征曲线下面积(area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, AUC)。研究结果:在78个养殖场中比较生物安全(63个集约化,15个粗放化)。通过横断面调查与统一化Biocheck.UGent变量比较,未显示系统间清楚分离。集约化与粗放化养殖场未分离成不同组,且未出现一致的系统水平模式。热图显示,集约化农场36个分类变量均有多于1个反应类别,粗放化农场34/36如此;粗放化农场仅有饲养密度和清空禽舍步骤数无变异。若干变量在两系统均呈持续高风险:饲料筒仓清洁与消毒、饲料运送频率、访客无禽期要求、与静水或流水邻近。其中水邻近和饲料运送频率反映固定环境或结构特征,其余与农场管理实践相关。在28个变量中,绝对后验均值系数最大的3个分类变量为尸体储存清洁、饲养密度和雏鸡运送频率。贝叶斯模型以集约化=0、粗放化=1编码生产系统,系数描述控制其他变量后各反应类别与生产系统的关联,不是因果效应;负系数表示与集约化农场关联,正系数表示与粗放化农场关联。尸体储存清洁方面,以“总是”清洁为参考,“有时”清洁后验均值系数为–2.38(95%可信区间[credible interval, CrI] –6.28至0.06;负系数后验概率0.93),提示该反应更常见于集约化农场,但95% CrI包括零;“从不”和“无独立尸体储存”接近零且区间宽。描述结果显示,61.9%(39/63)集约化农场报告“有时”清洁,粗放化农场为0/15;60.0%(9/15)粗放化农场报告“总是”清洁。饲养密度以“不超过33 kg/m”为参考,超过33 kg/m的后验均值系数为–3.22(95% CrI –7.05至0.02;负系数后验概率0.96),提示高密度在粗放化农场较少见,但95% CrI包括零;所有粗放化农场(15/15)密度不超过33 kg/m,71.4%(45/63)集约化农场超过该阈值。雏鸡运送频率以“少于3次”为参考,“3至6次”后验均值系数为+1.08(95% CrI –0.22至4.59;正系数后验概率0.80),提示粗放化农场更常处于中等频率,但方向支持较弱且95% CrI包括零;“超过6次”接近零。描述结果显示,93.3%(14/15)粗放化农场每年3至6次,65.1%(41/63)集约化农场超过6次。其余23个分类变量和雇佣人数后验均值接近零但可信区间宽,不能解释为系统间相似;经理经验每年系数较小(后验均值–0.05,95% CrI –0.14至0.01;负系数后验概率0.94)。近似PSIS-LOO交叉验证AUC为0.94,反映该数据集内农场分离而非可推广预测性能。时间敏感性分析显示集约化农场总体模式大致稳定,但若干变量在时期之间有描述性变化,尤其饲养密度、分多步清空禽舍、装卸区清洁消毒和经理经验。超过33 kg/m比例从2022年前78.7%(37/47)降至之后50.0%(8/16)。由于所有粗放化农场均在2022年后调查,模型无法完全分离时间和系统差异;将调查时期作为协变量后,超过33 kg/m系数从–3.22减弱至–1.31,而尸体储存清洁关联仍一致(调整前后–2.38和–2.82)。先验和模型敏感性分析对该3个变量估计大致相似;排除结构性系统关联变量后尸体储存清洁关联仍一致。讨论部分总结与结论翻译:讨论指出,本研究旨在识别荷兰肉鸡农场生物安全实施变异,并评估其是否系统性与生产系统相关。通过统一化Biocheck.UGent子集比较28个HPAI相关措施,发现有限证据支持生产系统间系统性差异,两组内均有显著变异。最大估计差异涉及尸体储存清洁消毒、饲养密度和雏鸡运送频率,但统计支持不一。近零系数不能因整体变异小解释;观察到的变异似乎分布在个体农场而非与生产系统一致,但仅15个粗放化农场且变量多,估计不精确,宽可信区间不能排除中等系统差异。若干措施在两系统均持续高风险,提示行业共同薄弱环节,包括饲料筒仓清洁、访客无禽期等,改善实施不太可能仅依赖意识。尸体储存清洁是唯一直接可修改管理实践且敏感性分析最一致;但尸体储存配置理解可能影响回答,荷兰家禽产业链质量方案(IKB Kip)允许尸体储存整合于禽舍而非物理独立设施。饲养密度是明确结构差异,绝大多数集约化超过33
